label: Development and life history
text: BI.O.A3.2 Development and life history. Development turns one cell into a patterned body. Differentiation is change in gene expression under position and history. Morphogen gradients and induction are mechanisms, not universal laws. A stem cell can self-renew and produce differentiated daughters; potency is a measured range. Life history covers growth, reproduction and ageing, with trade-offs as the claim. Evo-devo lives here and cites BI.O.A4.

warrant.standard: Controlled physiology or developmental perturbation; dose–response
